Information Management 1 | Final Project Instructions & Documentation Guide




                                     INFORMATION MANAGEMENT 1

                        Final Project Instructions
                         Two (2) Projects per Group | Academic Year 2025–2026

      Group Composition: 3 members per group · Both projects done and presented by the
                                       same team



   Project 1: Data Modeling & CRUD System
   Design a data model, then build a working PHP-based CRUD application



  1      Design a Complete Data Model
         Cover all three levels: Conceptual (entities & relationships), Logical (attributes & keys), and
         Physical (tables, data types, constraints).


  2      Implement as a Functional Web System
         Build a working PHP application that supports all four basic CRUD operations: Create, Read,
         Update, and Delete.


  3      Choose a PHP Coding Approach
         Object-Oriented (OOP), PDO, or Procedural (Preferred). Procedural PHP is recommended for
         this course level, but other approaches are also accepted.


  4      Prepare Documentation
         Include your ER diagram and a brief explanation of design decisions showing the relationship
         between your data model and the system.




   Project 2: Open-Source PHP Project Customization
   Find, study, customize, and present an existing PHP project



  1      Find a Suitable PHP Project
         Source from any reputable free repository. Suggested site: www.sourcecodester.com/php — or
         any other available open-source PHP repository.


  2      Study the Project Thoroughly
         Understand its code structure, database design, and how each module works before presenting
         it.




                            Academic Year 2025–2026 · Prepared by the Course Instructor
Information Management 1 | Final Project Instructions & Documentation Guide



  3       Customize or Enhance the Project
          Add UI improvements, a new feature or module, or adapt the system to a new use case. The
          group must demonstrate understanding, not just run the original source.


  4       Cite the Original Source
          Include the project title, author (if available), and URL clearly in your documentation and during
          your presentation.



General Requirements (Both Projects)
   Rules that apply to both projects
     • Each group must have exactly 3 members. Both projects are submitted and presented by the
          same team.
      •   Presentation may be done online or face-to-face on the instructor-assigned date. Each group
          must be ready to demo both projects live.
      •   Projects must run on a local server environment (e.g., XAMPP, WAMP, or Laragon) using a
          MySQL or MariaDB database.
      •   Submit all project files, database SQL files, and complete group documentation on or before
          the presentation date.
      •   All members must be able to explain and answer questions about both projects. Individual
          understanding will be part of the evaluation.




                             Academic Year 2025–2026 · Prepared by the Course Instructor
Information Management 1 | Final Project Instructions & Documentation Guide



                                        DOCUMENTATION GUIDE

                   What to Include in Your Submission
      This guide explains the expected contents, format, and structure of each section of your group
                                            documentation.


   Section 1: Project 1 — Data Model Documentation
   Show your understanding of data design before writing a single line of code



1.1 Cover Page
 Project Title                          Name of the system you built (e.g., Student Record Management
                                        System)
 Group Name / Number                    Your assigned group name or number
 Members                                Full name of each member and their assigned role
 Course & Section                       Information Management 1 — your section code
 Date Submitted                         Actual date of submission



1.2 System Overview
Write a short paragraph (3–5 sentences) describing what your system does, who will use it, and what
problem it solves. Keep it simple and direct.


1.3 Data Model
   Required diagrams and descriptions
     • Conceptual Model — Entity-Relationship Diagram (ERD) showing all entities and their
       relationships. Label cardinality (one-to-many, many-to-many, etc.).
     • Logical Model — Refined ERD with all attributes, primary keys (PK), and foreign keys (FK)
       identified.
     • Physical Model — Actual database schema showing table names, column names, data types
       (INT, VARCHAR, DATE, etc.), constraints (NOT NULL, UNIQUE, DEFAULT), and indexes.
     • Brief narrative — 1–2 paragraphs explaining your design decisions (why you chose those
       entities, how relationships are structured).



1.4 CRUD Functionality Description
For each module in your system, describe the four CRUD operations. Use the table format below as a
guide:


 Module / Table       Create                 Read                    Update              Delete
 e.g., Students       Add new student        View student list       Edit student info   Remove student
 (add more rows)




                           Academic Year 2025–2026 · Prepared by the Course Instructor
Information Management 1 | Final Project Instructions & Documentation Guide




1.5 Screenshots
Include at least one screenshot per CRUD operation (minimum 4 screenshots). Label each screenshot
clearly, e.g., "Figure 1: Add New Student Form."


1.6 Database SQL File
Attach or embed your exported SQL file (.sql). It must include both the CREATE TABLE statements and
sample INSERT data so the evaluator can restore and test the system.



   Section 2: Project 2 — Source Code Documentation
   Demonstrate that your group understands the project you chose, not just downloaded it



2.1 Project Information
 Project Title                         Exact title of the PHP project you chose
 Source / URL                          Full URL where the project was downloaded from
 Original Author                       Name of the original developer (if available)
 Type of System                        e.g., Inventory System, Hospital Management, Library System
 Technologies Used                     PHP version, MySQL, libraries, frameworks (if any)
 Customizations Made                   Brief summary of what your group changed or added



2.2 System Overview
Summarize what the system does in 3–5 sentences. Describe its main purpose and intended users. Then
explain why your group chose this particular project.


2.3 Module / Feature Walkthrough
   For each major module or feature of the project, provide:
     • Module name (e.g., User Login, Product Management, Report Generation)
     • Short description of what it does
     • Screenshot showing the module in action
     • Explanation of any customization or enhancement your group made to this module


2.4 Database Structure
Provide the ER Diagram or list of tables from the project's database. Include table names, column names,
and key fields. Even if you did not design it, you must understand and explain it.


2.5 Code Explanation
Pick two (2) important PHP files from the project. For each file:


                           Academic Year 2025–2026 · Prepared by the Course Instructor
Information Management 1 | Final Project Instructions & Documentation Guide



  • State the filename and its purpose
  • Paste a key code snippet (no more than 20 lines)
  • Explain what the code does in plain language


2.6 Customization / Enhancement Summary
   Describe what your group changed or added, including:
     • What feature or improvement was added
     • Why you made this change (purpose / benefit)
     • Before-and-after screenshots if applicable
     • Any challenges encountered and how you solved them



   Section 3: Group & Member Contributions
   Transparency in workload distribution is required for both projects



3.1 Group Information
 Group Name / Number                    Your assigned group designation
 Course & Section                       Information Management 1 — your section code
 Submission Date                        Date both projects are submitted
 Presentation Date                      Scheduled date and time of presentation
 Presentation Mode                      Online (video call) or Face-to-Face



3.2 Member Contribution Table
List every member’s name and their specific contributions to each project. Be specific — do not just write
“coding” or “presentation.”


 Member Name               Contributions to Project 1                   Contributions to Project 2
 Member 1 (Full Name)      e.g., ERD design, database creation,         e.g., Setup, module walkthrough,
                           login module                                 documentation

 Member 2 (Full Name)      e.g., CRUD forms (Create & Update), UI       e.g., Customization of inventory module,
                           layout                                       screenshots

 Member 3 (Full Name)      e.g., Read & Delete functions, testing,      e.g., Code explanation section,
                           SQL export                                   presentation slides



3.3 File Submission Checklist
   Make sure your submission folder or ZIP file includes all of the following:
    • Project 1 — All PHP source files and project folder

      •   Project 1 — SQL export file (.sql) with table structure and sample data
      •   Project 1 — Documentation (this guide, with all sections filled in)
      •   Project 2 — All PHP source files and project folder
      •   Project 2 — SQL export file (.sql) for the chosen project
      •   Project 2 — Documentation (Sections 2 and 3 of this guide)
      •   Presentation slides (if applicable)




   Section 4: Presentation Guide & Grading Rubric
   Criteria used to evaluate both projects during your final presentation



4.1 Presentation Format
 Duration                               20–30 minutes per group (both projects combined)
 Mode                                   Online (Google Meet / Zoom) or Face-to-Face
 Who Presents                           All 3 members must participate and speak during the presentation
 Demo Required                          Yes — live demo of both systems is required
 Q&A                                    5–10 minutes of questions; each member may be asked
                                        individually
 Language                               English, Filipino, or Bisaya — as instructed by your teacher



4.2 Suggested Presentation Flow
  1       Introduction (2–3 min)
          Introduce your group, state your group name, and briefly introduce both projects.


  2       Project 1 Demo & Explanation (8–10 min)
          Present your data model (ERD), walk through the system, and demonstrate each CRUD
          operation live.


  3       Project 2 Demo & Explanation (8–10 min)
          Present the chosen open-source project, explain its structure, highlight your customizations, and
          demo the system.


  4       Q&A and Wrap-Up (5–10 min)
          Answer questions from the instructor. Any member may be asked about any part of either
          project.
